exposure: Coronary artery lesions caused by Kawasaki disease
Myocardial involvement caused by Kawasaki disease
outcome: ST-T depression on Holter monitoring during pregnancy
Increase in isolated ventricular premature contractions during pregnancy
Preterm birth (less than 35 weeks of gestation)
cohort: The study included 39 patients with coronary artery lesions and myocardial involvement caused by Kawasaki disease, who had 67 deliveries at a single institution between 1991 and 2022.
finding: Pregnancy and delivery outcomes were favorable for patients without myocardial ischemia and involvement, even with stenotic lesions, but ventricular tachycardia can worsen and myocardial ischemia may occur in patients with myocardial involvement or coronary artery occlusions during pregnancy.
mod_finding: 74% of deliveries were vaginal (with 16 requiring assistance), and 26% were Caesarean sections (5 due to cardiac disease); Holter-electrocardiograms are helpful in deciding the management of pregnancy and mode of delivery.
